persona: Upset and chatty, uses exclamation marks, calms down once she knows what to do. Asked the shop for a copy of the heat pump invoice because the original was lost.
initial_message: I'm honestly so shaken!! On Friday night (the 11th) the wind snapped a huge branch off the tree in our back yard and it came crashing down right on top of the heat pump outside. The top is completely crushed and now the heat pump won't even turn on. Thank goodness nobody was out there. What do I do now??

facts.policyholder.name: Mere Kererumont
facts.incident.description: On Friday night strong wind snapped a large branch off the liquidambar tree in our back yard. It fell onto the heat pump outdoor unit beside the house and crushed the top. The heat pump has not worked since.
facts.incident.cause: Strong wind broke a branch off our own tree
facts.loss.description: Heat pump outdoor unit crushed on top and its fan grille bent in; the heat pump no longer turns on
facts.if_asked_about_heating: We are using a plug-in heater in the lounge for now. The house is fine to live in.
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Turned the heat pump off at the isolating switch on Saturday morning; my brother cut up the branch and moved it off the unit

facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the branch on the heat pump, taken on Saturday morning. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Nikau Ridge Sparks, total $4,427.50 including GST, dated 15 September 2026. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: A reprint of the heat pump invoice from Harakeke By Appliances. We bought it on 7 June 2023; the store printed this copy on 14 September 2026 because I could not find the original. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_dates: We bought the heat pump on 7 June 2023. The store reprinted the invoice for me on 14 September because I could not find the original.

design.notes: Innocent control: the heat pump invoice was reprinted on 14 September 2026, after the storm on 11 September 2026; the purchase date, 7 June 2023, is not. Only the purchase date counts (rules, section 3).

triage.rationale: Wind damage to a fixed heat pump at the insured address, nobody hurt, home habitable, photo and a complete quote (NZD 4,427.50 including GST), policy on file. The invoice reprint date (14 September) is after the storm, but only the purchase date (7 June 2023) counts. Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Purchase date 7 June 2023 is before the incident; the reprint date 14 September 2026 is ignored

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 May 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2021-05-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
